flags.purpose: Retrieves system-wide exploit protection policies such as DEP, ASLR, SEHOP, CFG and others.
flags.security_use_case: Audit global exploit protection posture of the OS.
flags.threat_detected: Disabled exploit mitigations exposing system to memory corruption and ROP attacks.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Shows defaults that may differ from per-app settings.
flags.safe_followup: Use Set-ProcessMitigation or Windows Security Exploit Protection to enable protections.

flags.purpose: Shows actual mitigations applied to currently running instances of a process.
flags.security_use_case: Verify browsers, document readers, and user-facing apps run with strong protections.
flags.threat_detected: Applications running without DEP/ASLR/CFG vulnerable to drive-by exploits.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Runtime state may differ from registry configuration.
flags.safe_followup: Harden with Set-ProcessMitigation and restart the application.

flags.purpose: Exports full mitigation policy for all applications from registry.
flags.security_use_case: Compliance audit and baseline comparison across systems.
flags.threat_detected: Applications missing exploit protections creating weak points.
flags.risk_if_misused: None; read-only. Large output requires parsing.
flags.safe_followup: Compare against CIS baseline and enable missing mitigations.

flags.purpose: Reads mitigation settings from an exported XML policy file.
flags.security_use_case: Analyze policies from other systems before applying them.
flags.threat_detected: Weak policies imported from untrusted systems.
flags.risk_if_misused: Review file carefully before applying; may reduce security if misused.
flags.safe_followup: Validate XML, then apply using Set-ProcessMitigation if trusted.

flags.purpose: Shows mitigation settings for a specific running process by PID.
flags.security_use_case: Investigate target process for exploit protection posture.
flags.threat_detected: Process with disabled mitigations susceptible to exploitation.
flags.risk_if_misused: Process may exit before action; settings are runtime view.
flags.safe_followup: Harden policy and restart process if required.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Finds applications lacking critical DEP or ASLR protections.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Identifies high-risk applications vulnerable to memory exploits.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Correlates running processes with Control Flow Guard status.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detects processes running without CFG which prevents code reuse attacks.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Single-pane summary of system exploit protections.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Quick verification of OS exploit protection baseline.
